title: Compact action token matrix for dark-brand variants and chart label contrast
creator: Liam O'Neill
description:
Problem: Several console surfaces show inconsistent CTA/button appearance in dark branded themes (customer-specific accent palettes). Charts and small table labels occasionally fall below recommended contrast when brand tints are applied as button accents. This causes visual inconsistency across components and a handful of accessibility violations in our automated checks.

Goal: Produce a compact token matrix and component override guidance that: (1) anchors button surfaces and outlines to neutral surface tokens in dark mode, (2) defines a deterministic brand-accent tint blending strategy for compact/dense controls, and (3) includes explicit contrast-preserving remaps for chart labels and table badges when brand accents are applied. The output should be implementable as token data + a small component-level override layer (no runtime color computation on the client).

Scope: Compact buttons (primary/secondary/ghost in compact density), small table badges, chart axis/label/legend text for brand variants, and the console shared token map. Not covering large marketing pages or legacy static rails.

Constraints and non-goals: Must avoid runtime heavy color math in the browser. Avoid changing existing token names used by third-party integrators. This is a design token mapping and override matrix; engineering will implement via build-time token transforms and CSS variable fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: New token matrix documented in Confluence with explicit mapping rows for compact primary/secondary/ghost buttons across neutral, brand-soft, and brand-strong variants
Contrast: all button label colors and small chart/table label colors meet WCAG AA (4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text where applicable) in dark-brand test palettes
Figma components updated with variant previews (three brand tints + neutral) and a compact density test page
Engineering sign-off on token format (JSON input) and fallback rules; sample build step that emits CSS variables validated
Automated a11y test added to console-styling pipeline that validates the three canonical brand palettes against the new tokens
steps: Audit current compact button tokens and identify where brand accent is applied (DESIGN + console-styling audit) - 2d

Define blending and anchoring rules: prefer surface-anchored tints for backgrounds, outline anchored to border tokens, and label color computed from anchored text token with preserve-contrast modifier - 3d
Create a flat token matrix file (design JSON) with keys: compact.primary.bg, compact.primary.fg, compact.ghost.bg, compact.ghost.border, chart.label.brand-remap, table.badge.brand-remap
Update Figma components and produce screenshot gallery for three brand tints and neutral in dark frame
Write Confluence spec with examples, export token JSON and unit contrast report, and add to PR description
Work with frontend eng to produce build-time transform that consumes token JSON and emits CSS vars and a small override layer
Ship guarded feature flag behind console-theme.beta and run on small customer subset for telemetry (latency/renders)
engineering_notes: Implementation notes for ENG: use a build-time token transform; avoid runtime color mixing. Token precedence: explicit brand-anchored tokens > compact density tokens > base component tokens > legacy fallback. Provide three token keys per semantic (base, brand-soft, brand-strong) so we don't compute blends at runtime. For chart labels, add chart.label.brand-remap token that engineers can map to axis text at render time. Add unit tests that run axe+contrast check using the three canonical brand palettes. Example PR template: link design JSON, include visual diff slate, add accessibility report. See sample PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/12234
